record.file_problem: Repository metadata and README/file list only; code was not read or run.
record.tranche_reason: The README reports a capability benchmark of an abliterated checkpoint and discusses what it can and cannot show about preserved capability. It does not reproduce the original direction measurement or refusal intervention.
record.gate_note: The README's refusal-rate figures (64–99% and 0–6%) are attributed to the publisher's model card, so they are not rows. The repository's SWE-bench result is included because the README explicitly interprets it as evidence about retained coding ability. Other serving, latency, and retrieval measurements are not direct tests of the claim versions.
record.test_reason: This is a serving and benchmarking playbook for a publisher's abliterated checkpoint. The repository measures throughput, latency, NIAH retrieval and one SWE-bench Pro score. It never measures refusal: the refusal rates (64–99% to 0–6%, ≤1.7% with thinking on), the MMLU/GSM8K deltas and Sapwell's HarmBench and KL figures are all cited from the publisher or a third party. Its only capability result has no matched non-abliterated control; the base comparison differs in quantization and runtime, and the authors say it cannot isolate abliteration's cost. The study relies on the abliterated model as a tool and reports its own serving performance, so it tests no version.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct. The authors say the 85% vs 75% gap confounds abliteration with quantization and runtime. It supports only that abliteration did not gut agentic coding ability. A same-lane non-abliterated NVFP4 control is still missing. They also stress the repository documents serving and benchmarking only, and that all refusal figures come from the publisher's card.
record.recipe_differences: This is a serving and benchmarking playbook for a publisher-provided abliterated checkpoint, not a replication of the original direction-finding or ablation method.
record.method_sensitivity: The README says the base comparison uses different quantization and runtime, preventing attribution of the score difference to abliteration.

fits_no_version.finding: Abliterated Qwen3.8-27B NVFP4 resolved 34/40 on a SWE-bench Pro subset. Base Qwen3.8-27B (Q4_K_M, llama.cpp) resolved 30/40. The comparison is confounded by quantization and runtime.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: An abliterated checkpoint keeps agentic coding ability (unmatched comparison; does not isolate abliteration's effect).

record.problems: No non-abliterated control on the same lane; the base-model comparison changes both quantization and runtime. The refusal-rate figures are cited from the publisher's card rather than measured by this repository.
record.rows_left_out: Publisher-card refusal and capability figures were left out because they are cited results, not results reported from this repository's own tests. Serving-path, throughput, latency, and NIAH measurements were left out because they do not directly test the claim versions.

untested.parts: Direction extraction, ablation, addition, refusal rates and matched capability retention are not measured by the repository.
No refusal evaluation of the weight-edited release; refusal figures are cited from the publisher's card and Sapwell's benchmarking.
The claim that thinking does not restore refusals rests on publisher-card numbers, not the repository's own measurement. Only the 9.11 vs 9.9 capability toggle was measured.

record.verdict_notes: The reader's 'tests'/T2 and its V1 limits_scope label are overturned. The study measures no refusal behaviour or direction, and its capability comparison is explicitly uncontrolled. Cited figures (publisher card, Sapwell: 82% HarmBench compliance, KL 0.04–0.08, FP8 build) are correctly left out as rows.

versions.untested_parts: The benchmark bears only on capability retention. The README does not test the difference-in-means direction, its ablation or addition, refusal behavior, or other abilities beyond the reported coding benchmark.
No refusal evaluation of the weight-edited release is reported by the repository; the cited refusal figures come from the publisher's card.
No attack suppression or training against ablation is tested.
No alternative direction geometry or multiplicity is tested.
No harmfulness judgment or refusal-decision representation is tested.
No transfer across languages, model variants, or training stages is tested.
No refusal-training procedure or training-stage comparison is tested.
The README notes that the benchmark used thinking on but does not test whether the refusal-direction claim holds in reasoning models.
